read_this_first: A vertex group is a BONE DEFORM group if its name matches an armature bone; otherwise it is a CLASSIFICATION group (CL_ prefix). Classification groups are now ONE GARMENT PIECE EACH — the old CL_Shorts/CL_Accessories catch-alls were split 2026-08-05. Check "islands" before operating on any group anyway. || RULES ARE NOW THE TOP-LEVEL 'rules' KEY (moved from GARMENT_EDITING_PROCEDURE on 2026-08-14). See 'rules_meta' for the numbering contract and a keyword index.
rules: 1. The garment pieces are DOUBLE-WALLED shells (outer surface + inner lining, ~0.0175 apart). Their two walls sit at DIFFERENT distances from the body by definition.
2. NEVER fit vertices to an absolute target gap and iterate. Converging every vertex on one number is mathematically identical to collapsing the shell to zero thickness. ONE PASS ONLY.

3. Move shells with a WIDE-RADIUS VECTOR blur (band 0.12, shorts 0.09), not a scalar blur and not a narrow one. Each vertex moves along the body normal at ITS OWN nearest point; on curvy or concave regions neighbours get different directions and the walls SHEAR past each other. A wide vector field makes the piece translate instead of shear.
4. NEVER use a plain Shrinkwrap modifier — it projects each vertex independently and flattens the shell.

5. Clearance against the body must be sampled at FACE CENTRES and EDGE MIDPOINTS, not vertices. Faces are ~0.1 units across; the body pokes through the middle of a face while all four corners sit safely outside.
6. Verification is FACE-vs-FACE overlap (BVHTree.overlap) compared against the ORIGINAL mesh, never vertex-to-surface distance. Two surfaces intersect while every vertex stays far apart.
7. Self-intersection is DIRECTIONAL: identify which face is the inner wall (smaller gap) and push the pair APART. Smoothing does not fix it and oscillates.
8. Any iterative repair must TRACK THE BEST STATE and restore it — corrections accumulate and diverge after the real defects clear. Cap cumulative per-vertex drift (0.018 worked).
9. Hidden geometry needs no visual-quality constraints. Demanding full body clearance UNDER an opaque band while also requiring the shorts stay inside it left an unsatisfiable 2.6mm window.
10. Use each vertex's LOCAL nearest band vertex as a ceiling, not the band's global minimum.
11. Rigid ornaments (CL_Buckle) must be TRANSLATED as one unit. Copying per-vertex displacement from the nearest band vertex deforms them into the band.
12. ALWAYS capture a baseline screenshot of the ORIGINAL mesh at the same camera before judging an artefact. Three times the suspected defect turned out to be pre-existing.

13. "Not intersecting" is NOT the same as "on top of". Zero face overlaps only means two pieces do not cross; one can still sit entirely BEHIND the other. For layering, compare GAP-TO-BODY locally: the outer piece must be further from the body than the inner piece.

14. Do NOT test occlusion with nearest-point surface normals. On a hanging piece (the groin flap) the nearest point for some vertices is on its INNER face, which reports "behind" forever — an iterative push chasing that ran the buckle 0.32 units into empty space.
15. Compute a rigid shift ANALYTICALLY where possible instead of iterating to a condition. For the buckle: shift = max over its verts of (local max flap gap + margin - own gap), one pass.
16. Verify group CONTENTS, not group NAMES — the CL_SidePanel_* groups were actually the bead cords. Test what geometry does (how many beads it threads), not where it sits.

17. NEVER edit geometry while Blender is in Edit or Sculpt Mode. The object-level mesh you read and write is a stale copy; leaving the mode overwrites your edits from the mode-local copy. A hash comparison of the two copies proves nothing — it only says they match at that instant, not what gets written back. FORCE Object Mode at the start of every geometry operation.
18. bpy.data.is_dirty is UNRELIABLE here — it stays True after a verified successful save. Verify saves by checking the file mtime and size actually changed, not by the operator message.

19. Check your MEASUREMENT assumptions before believing a bad result. Three false alarms this session: "closer to tilted than seated" (neither matched — an exact 0.00000 was the real proof), a phantom 1.13-unit cord jump (assumed vertex indices were contiguous; bmesh deletion renumbers), and a hem-curl test that only looked at the boundary loop and missed the roll inverting.

20. Nearest-bone classification CUTS ACROSS PHYSICAL OBJECTS and has been wrong four times: cords labelled side panels, strand beads split into LegWrap/Anklet, 23 more labelled Bracelet, and CL_Shorts lumping six pieces. Classify by what geometry DOES (what threads what, what connects to what), never by name or by which bone is nearest.
21. Neighbour-interpolation fixes need a BOUNDED radius. An unbounded "or nearest 3" fallback dragged 55 bracelet and 18 anklet beads along with the hip strands.

22. An inward-only correction with a NARROW blur is required when a rim is already tighter than target while the band below it is loose — a wide blur averages the two and they cancel. This is what made the first corset-chest fix do nothing.

23. The clothes mesh has ONE material and one UV atlas. Colour differences (gold buckle, blue cloth, beads) come from the TEXTURE, not material slots — so material index cannot be used to identify a piece, and recolouring means editing the atlas or adding a slot (which costs a draw call).

24. "Zero intersections" between eyelid and eyeball is a DEGENERATE target - it is satisfied by the lid closing over the eye. It only became safe once the socket made the aperture a topological hole. Always verify the aperture is still open (count unobstructed eyeball faces), never trust the intersection count alone.

25. Compressing a volume against a DISTANCE FIELD collapses it. Squashing loc depth along the body normal flattened the hair tubes into shards. Retracting along each strand axis preserved the tubes but pushed roots sideways into deeper skull. What worked: DELETE the buried geometry (invisible anyway), then clamp and cap the remainder.

26. Procedural texture bakes: differentiating in texture space crosses UV island borders and invents slopes. Feather the applied slope to zero over ~5px inside the mask - a hard cut makes the cut edge itself the artifact. And every falloff must be smoothstep: a clipped parabola has a derivative discontinuity, and normals ARE the derivative, so the kink draws a ridge.

27. Do NOT transfer objects between .blend files with bpy.data.libraries.load - the loaded object arrives without its parent and its transform is wrong (observed: scale (0.01,0.01,0.01) instead of (0.72,0.008,0.62), which then made a fit compute a 36.7x scale to compensate). To recover a state, OPEN the file and redo the work there.

28. Put SANITY ASSERTS on computed transforms before applying them (e.g. assert 0.5 < scale < 2.0, assert |translation| < 0.1). Three separate times a mislocated object produced an absurd fit that was only caught by eye afterwards.

29. Turning off viewport overlays hides the TRANSFORM GIZMO along with everything else - it will look like gizmos are broken in Edit Mode. Leave overlays ON; hide the armature temporarily instead if a clean screenshot is needed, and restore it afterwards.
30. Measure the available UV TEXEL DENSITY of a region before designing texture detail for it. The eyeliner attempt burned several passes on a 16x50 texel canvas that could never hold it.

31. FACE GEOMETRY: build a rough strip and HAND IT TO STEPHANIE to seat by hand. Procedural seating around the eye socket failed three separate ways in one session (nearest-point grabbing the sleeve, normals flipping between three surfaces, chords crossing ridges) and each attempt cost more than it was worth. Set her up - unlock the target, lock everything else, hide the armature, frame the view - and hand over. Do not iterate.

32. BVHTree.find_nearest returns an UNSIGNED distance. A vertex buried 0.36mm UNDER the skin reports exactly the same clearance as one floating 0.36mm above it. A check built on it will read burial as success (this produced a strip that rendered as a dashed line). Use a SIGNED test: dot(p - nearest_loc, nearest_normal), or ray-cast outward and see if anything is hit.

33. Yemoja_Body contains SKIN, EYEBALLS AND SOCKET SLEEVES in one mesh. Within ~1mm of the aperture all three are candidates for 'nearest face', and their normals point in genuinely different directions, so as a point moves the nearest face flips and an iterative push along normals DIVERGES (observed runaway to 0.51 units before an assert caught it). Seat radially from the eye centre using ray casts instead - a ray asks a question with an unambiguous answer, nearest-point does not.

34. The two lash objects have base geometry on OPPOSITE sides of the mirror plane: Yemoja_LashCards_Top_R is on -x, Yemoja_LashCards_Bottom_R is on +x, each with a Mirror modifier generating the other side. Detect the side from mean vertex X against the plane (-0.0044) and pick the matching eye centre. Assuming the wrong one put lash 'roots' 0.2883 from the eye centre against a 0.061 radius.

35. Face detail is a CLOSE-UP-ONLY investment. At fighting-game camera distance the whole face is a few pixels and no facial feature reads at all, regardless of colour or contrast. Judge facial art on select-screen / portrait / victory-cam framing, and justify its vertex cost on those surfaces - not on gameplay legibility.

36. 'Arc length' computed as the sum of gaps between consecutive scattered points is NOT a path length. The lash root cloud gave 0.75 by that measure against a true fitted-curve length of 0.11 and a chord of 0.099 - inflated ~7x by zigzag. Fit a smooth curve through the cloud first, then measure and resample along the fit. Sweeping a continuous strip through raw scattered points also inherits every wobble as a visible kink.

37. LOWER lash roots must be identified by distance to the EYE CENTRE, not distance to skin. Lower lashes splay down toward the cheek, so their tips can sit nearer the skin than their roots do - the same trap as seating the lower lash line to 'nearest skin' and landing on the cheek.

38. Do NOT derive eyeball gaze by weighting vertices on texture darkness/saturation. At 97 verts the painted pupil is SMALLER THAN THE VERTEX SPACING, so the method finds whatever dark texels happen to sit near a vertex. It reported a 0.0 deg residual on a fix that was ~5.8 deg wrong, and Stephanie caught it by eye. Ask her to SELECT the iris faces and take the direction from those face centres - that is ground truth and costs one message.

39. Perceived gaze is the iris's position within the VISIBLE APERTURE, not the eyeball's axis. An eye aimed perfectly at the viewer still reads as staring past them if the lids sit such that the iris rides high in the opening. Measure iris-minus-aperture, not the axis alone.

40. ANATOMY: orbital axes diverge (~23 deg total in humans), so an eye genuinely focused on the viewer has its iris NASAL of its aperture centre - here 6.45 deg. Do NOT 'centre' the iris in the opening; that IS the wall-eyed look. This nearly caused a revert to the divergent state that started the session.

41. Eyeballs were on the SKIN material with texture-driven roughness, rendering matte - the 'dead doll' look. Eye realism is a MATERIAL problem before a paint problem (see rule on catchlights). Give eyes their own low-roughness material or paint smoothness into their atlas island.

42. Both eyeballs share an IDENTICAL UV bbox (0.5998-0.7647, 0.1022-0.2669). One paint edit hits both eyes. Vertical shifts are fine; a horizontal shift moves both irises the SAME way in texture space and breaks convergence.

43. Assert the SIGN of any hand-written rotation matrix before applying it - probe a known vector and check which way it goes. A pitch matrix intended to look down pitched up instead; the assert caught it before it touched the mesh.

44. In EDIT mode, mesh.uv_layers.active.data and similar base-mesh arrays read as EMPTY - the live data is in the edit-mesh. Use bmesh.from_edit_mesh() and bm.loops.layers.uv.active, or the read silently fails.

45. Do not chase a residual eyeball dent with more smoothing. Taubin took 0.60mm -> 0.46mm; pushing further erodes the rebuilt corneal curve, and projecting the sclera to a true sphere is what previously drove socket intersections 94 -> 194. The residual is a hand-sculpt call.

46. When subdividing or editing a symmetric region on BOTH sides, derive the second side by MIRROR-MATCHING the first side's faces, never by re-running the same angular/geometric selection per side. Independent selection gave 194 vs 197 verts and silently broke the mirror symmetry this body was rebuilt to have.

47. A round shape painted in the atlas renders FACETED if it spans only a few faces - UV interpolates affinely within each face. Before repainting a small feature, check how many faces it covers. The pupil was round in the texture (axis ratio 0.926) and still read as an angular blob at 2 faces across.

48. Before writing into any atlas RECTANGLE, verify no other UV island intrudes on it - the bbox of an island is not the island. Check every loop whose UV falls inside the rect and confirm it belongs to the intended geometry.

49. A catchlight landing ON the pupil fragments it and destroys the focused read. Portrait convention puts it in the upper iris around 10 or 2 o'clock, overlapping the limbus. This makes the SELECT-SCREEN KEY LIGHT DIRECTION a gameplay-facing decision: the same mesh reads focused or vacant depending on it.

50. Eyes not reading as 'set into the face' is usually the MISSING UPPER-LID SHADOW, not the eye itself. Real lids overhang and shade the top of the eyeball; without that the eye reads as a bright sphere resting on a mask. It can be faked in the atlas for zero verts and zero draw calls.

51. When the WHOLE image is wrong in one direction (too blue, too flat, too dull), check the VIEW TRANSFORM before touching lamps or materials. Colour management is the last step in the chain, so a wrong choice there masquerades as a lighting or material fault. AgX desaturates by design; on a low-saturation blue/white character that reads as a clinical sci-fi cast. Khronos PBR Neutral holds midtone saturation while still rolling highlights off - use it for judging skin and the wet eye. A global cast almost always has a global cause.

52. Sun lamps are DISTANCE-INDEPENDENT: one rig reads correctly from full-body to single-vertex zoom with no retuning. Area lights fall off with distance squared and must be retuned per framing - the old rig's two fills at 350W and 45W were the fingerprint of exactly that. Working rig = suns. Beauty/screenshot rig = area lights, and only those, because only an area light gives a SHAPED catchlight; a sun's highlight is a dot because the sun is a dot.

53. A roughness-0.05 cornea MIRRORS THE ENVIRONMENT, not just the lamps. The sky's bright horizon band reflected as a hard bar straight across the pupil - a rule-49 violation with no lamp at fault. Corollary to rule 49: the select-screen ENVIRONMENT/skybox is a gameplay-facing decision too, not just the key-light direction. Verify by zeroing the world strength: if the artefact vanishes, it was the environment.

54. Ground Albedo in the Sky Texture node creates NO ground and casts NO bounce - it is a parameter inside the atmospheric simulation that brightens the lower sky. With no ground plane the character receives zero light from below, and a figure lit only from above against a black void reads as a specimen in a lab. Fake real ground bounce with a SHADOW-DISABLED sun at NEGATIVE elevation, warm (~4000K), at roughly 10% of key strength. Shadows must be off: a single upward shadow-caster produces horror-movie uplighting, because real bounce arrives from the whole floor at once.

55. Blender 5.2 API renames that will silently break older scripts: sky_type NISHITA -> MULTIPLE_SCATTERING; dust_density -> aerosol_density; the Background node's OUTPUT socket is named 'Background', not 'Color'. Also view_transform and look are OCIO-driven DYNAMIC enums - bl_rna introspection returns only ['NONE'] even while the current value is 'AgX', so you cannot list them; probe by assignment inside a try/except.

56. A lamp's Color swatch MULTIPLIES with the Kelvin temperature_color. When use_temperature is enabled, set Color to pure white or the two stack and the hue becomes impossible to reason about. Kelvin runs opposite to intuition: LOWER Kelvin = warmer, because the number describes how hot the emitter physically is and hotter bodies glow bluer.

57. Keep every non-exporting helper NESTED under PREVIEW_LIGHTS rather than in sibling top-level collections, so the single export-exclusion rule keeps covering everything. A '_Staging' collection was holding two lights and a camera that the PREVIEW_LIGHTS rule did not cover - the rule and the scene had silently drifted apart. Current structure: PREVIEW_LIGHTS > {_review_cam, LIGHTS_Working, LIGHTS_Beauty}.

58. To flatten exposure falloff across a subject, move the light BACK and turn it UP: distance 4 -> 7 needs about 3x the wattage ((7/4)^2) and buys a far gentler chest-vs-face gradient. A near area light blows out whatever is closest to it - the beauty bounce card at z 4.9 lit her chest two stops hotter than her face until it was moved.

59. URP Lit CANNOT READ VERTEX COLOURS. Any colour authored as a colour attribute is invisible in Unity, and Blender's FBX exporter only ships the ACTIVE attribute anyway. Bake to the atlas or use a texture. Cost this session: Yemoja_Lips was a 73-step vertex gradient that could never have reached Unity.

60. A material slot holding ZERO FACES still exports as a Unity material and a wasted draw call. Audit faces-per-slot (not just slot count) before every export. Yemoja_Body carried an empty 'Yemoja_Lashes' slot left over from the lash rebuild.

61. A loaded image is NOT a connected image. Check inputs['Base Color'].is_linked, not whether the texture appears in the material. Yemoja_Hair had its base colour texture loaded TWICE and plugged in NEITHER time.
62. Grade a texture against the range the MESH's UVs actually reference, not the whole image. Unused atlas padding skews the min/max and drags the mapping off.

63. Diffuse albedo above ~0.9 linear is not physical. To read as white, lift the MIDPOINT and let lighting supply the rest; forcing the mean to 0.9 forces you to crush contrast to avoid clipping. Hair graded to mean 0.75 linear kept 95% of its strand variation.

64. Duplicate image datablocks: check which one is USED before deleting. The clean-named one may be the orphan. Clothes_BaseColor_Ocean2 had zero users while Clothes_BaseColor_Ocean2.001 was the live one. Remap, then purge; never delete by name.

65. VERIFY AN FBX BY RE-IMPORTING AND READING IT. The exporter's success message is not evidence. Import into a throwaway scene, read vert counts / bones / materials / colour attributes, then remove exactly what was added.

66. Blender material names BECOME Unity material names. Name them to the target project's convention (Yemoja_*_mat) BEFORE export, not after, or Unity generates a parallel set and the prefab's material array indices shift.

67. STANDARD DEVIATION DOES NOT MEAN DETAIL. Split a texture by spatial frequency before deciding it is worth keeping: block-average at 128px and compare that std against the total. Hair base colour was 84% low-frequency (blotches); its normal map was 0.4% (real detail). Grading preserved the blotches faithfully and Stephanie spotted them instantly on the back of the head.

68. THIS MODELLER PAINTS FLAT-FILL ATLASES. Assume base colour and roughness maps carry NO detail until measured - both hair maps had ~30% of the image sitting in one histogram bin. The NORMAL map is usually the only one with real information. Same disease previously found in the clothes atlas.
69. Dropping a blotchy map is a MOBILE WIN, not a compromise. Hair went from three 2048 maps to one 1024 normal map by replacing base colour and roughness with constants.

70. SKIN WEIGHTS CAN BE MIRRORED ONTO THE WRONG-SIDE BONES AND NOTHING WILL TELL YOU. Yemoja_Body has 23 .L groups but only 2 carry any weight: total weight .L = 13.25 vs .R = 4098.14. Both halves of the body are skinned to the RIGHT bones. Bind pose looks perfect; it only breaks once a non-symmetric animation plays. Yemoja_Clothes on the SAME rig is correctly sided (L 2159 / R 2082), which is what proves it is a fault and not a convention.

71. TEST WEIGHT SIDEDNESS BY SUMMING TOTAL WEIGHT PER SIDE, not by checking that .L groups exist. Existence proved nothing here - the groups were present and empty. Also probe individual mirrored vertices: a vert at +x and its partner at -x must report DIFFERENT dominant bones.

72. Attributing vertices to bones by DOMINANT VERTEX GROUP can hide asymmetry, because it inherits whatever the weights say. Cross-check geometric edits by the SIGN OF X instead - Stephanie's edits showed 387 verts moved at -x and 387 at +x, i.e. genuinely symmetric, while the bone attribution had made them look right-side-only.

73. A mesh's local Z is not world Z when the object carries a translation. Yemoja_Body sits at world offset (-0.0044, 0.1074, 4.0545) - measuring anatomy at raw local Z silently returns empty selections.

74. MIRROR-PAIR VERTICES IN LOCAL SPACE, NOT WORLD SPACE. Yemoja_Body's symmetry plane is local x=0, which sits at world x=-0.0044 (conventions.mirror_plane_world_x). Pairing partners in world coordinates offsets every match by TWICE that: 0.0088 units = 2.09 mm. That is large enough to blow a 1e-3 tolerance and small enough to look like genuine asymmetry, so it reads as a modelling fault rather than a coordinate-space bug. The same mesh measured in LOCAL space pairs 6528 verts with a worst gap of 5.9e-7. Companion to rule 73: the object's translation breaks X pairing as well as Z measurement.

75. A WORKSPACE TAB SWITCH CAN SILENTLY RESTORE EDIT MODE. Blender associates a mode with each workspace, so jumping to the Image Editor and back left Yemoja_Body in Edit Mode with no warning. The rule-1 Object Mode guard belongs at the TOP OF EVERY WRITE SCRIPT, not once per session.

76. DERIVE A GAZE AXIS FROM DIRECTIONS, NOT FROM AVERAGED POSITIONS. Averaging the 3D positions of the iris loops and taking centre->centroid reported a 3.82 deg DIVERGENCE that does not exist; the UV mapping is distorted, so the sampled cap is lopsided and its centroid tilts. Point-sampling the iris-centre UV, and the area-weighted mean of UNIT direction vectors, both give ~0.2-0.6 deg convergence and agree with each other. Because the mesh and atlas are mirrored, the bias came out equal-and-opposite on the two eyes - a mirrored ARTEFACT is indistinguishable from a mirrored BUG by symmetry alone. Always cross-check with a second estimator.

77. THE MIRRORED ATLAS IS SAFE FOR RADIALLY SYMMETRIC PAINT AND UNSAFE FOR DIRECTIONAL PAINT. The iris and pupil mirror harmlessly; a CATCHLIGHT does not - it lands on opposite sides of the two eyes and reads as two light sources. Anything directional painted into a mirrored island must sit ON the mirror axis, or the island must be un-mirrored. Stephanie caught this by eye before any measurement was taken.

78. DO NOT MOVE A PAINTED HIGHLIGHT AS AN ADDITIVE DIFFERENCE. Extracting it as (original - clean) yields the difference between white and teal, which is PINK, and adding that over a black pupil tints it. Erase with a donor at the SAME RADIUS (mirror about the pupil axis preserves both the radial structure and the vertical lid-shadow gradient) and repaint the highlight as an alpha composite with a fixed tone.

79. AN IN-MEMORY CHANGE MADE OVER MCP CAN REVERT BETWEEN CALLS. Creating the eye bones succeeded and reported 94 bones and 382 verts assigned; the next call found 92 bones, no eye vertex groups, and the original weights restored - a clean atomic rollback, cause never established (viewport undo or the add-on's undo handling around a mode toggle). It was verifying in a SEPARATE CALL that caught it; a same-call check would have reported success and been correct at that instant. Therefore: SAVE TO DISK inside the same call that makes a structural change, and always verify in a separate call afterwards.

80. PLACE AN EYE BONE AT THE SPHERE-FIT CENTRE, NEVER THE BOUNDING-BOX CENTRE. The corneal bulge drags the bbox centre forward, and a displaced pivot makes the eye wobble in the socket rather than rotate in it. Verify by rotating the bone and re-fitting the sphere: centre drift must be 0. Accept the resulting L/R asymmetry when the mesh carries a world offset (rule 73) - pivot accuracy beats rig symmetry, but exclude those bones from Symmetrize.

81. use_visible=True silently drops ANY object hidden for viewport work - including the armature. Before every export, list everything hidden in the view layer and unhide all of it except lights and cameras. Then confirm the re-import actually contains an ARMATURE and non-zero weights: a skeleton-less FBX exports without error or warning.

82. A strand atlas whose RGB is a uniform constant is an ALPHA-ONLY MASK and can be reused by any hair of that colour at zero material cost. Check RGB std before assuming a new hair type needs its own material. Colour lives per-texel; a shader tint node cannot vary within one material.

83. Parametrise a hair-card spine by TRUE ARC LENGTH, never by projection onto a straight axis. Equal steps in projection space spread cards apart wherever the curve bends, producing gaps that look like a density problem and are not.
84. Distribute cards at RANDOM offsets across the hair's thickness. Fixed rows read as parallel stripes no matter how many you use.

85. A painted base layer must sit INSIDE the card silhouette. Distance to the card point cloud includes tips that arc off the surface, so an isotropic falloff paints a halo above the hair. Also skip any solid root band at the base of the strand atlas (v < 0.05) whenever the card root is not hidden by other geometry.

86. Rule 30's texel-density check applies to NORMAL MAPS too, not just colour. A normal map carrying detail finer than its texel density does not degrade gracefully - it aliases into structured bands that look exactly like modelling faults. Yemoja's lips carried real normal detail (R std 0.074) across an 88-texel-wide region at ~2.1 texels/mm, i.e. roughly one texel per striation, and it rendered as hard lines across the lower lip.

87. A MIRRORED UV ATLAS PLUS ANY NORMAL-MAP DETAIL DRAWS A SEAM down the mirror line. The red channel encodes sideways slope and the tangent frame flips across the fold, so the two halves light in opposite directions. Either taper red to zero near the mirror line or keep that region's normal flat. This is why the line runs down her philtrum and chin, not just the lips.

88. UNIFORM ROUGHNESS READS AS PLASTIC. Vary it. Low-frequency roughness breakup (3D wave noise, wavelength >= 3mm so it stays above Nyquist at low texel density) is the cheapest anti-plastic tool available and, being a scalar, is immune to the mirrored-atlas problem in rule 87.

89. bpy.data.images.new() creates a GENERATED image. Setting .pixels and calling .save() writes the generated fill - a BLACK 2048 PNG - not your buffer, with no error. Copy an existing FILE-backed image datablock instead (src.copy()), foreach_set, .update(), then .save(). Both bad files were byte-identical and the same size; only reading back from disk caught it.

90. CUSTOM SPLIT NORMALS GO STALE the moment the geometry under them changes - resculpt, subdivide, sculpt. Blender does not update them and nothing warns you. Yemoja's lips were deviating 11.34 deg mean / 44.32 deg max from true smooth shading. Re-neutralise or re-transfer after ANY geometry change, and feather over 2 vertex rings so no shading edge appears at the boundary.

91. ON A MIRROR-SYMMETRIC SURFACE THE TRUE TANGENT NORMAL AT THE FOLD HAS A ZERO U-COMPONENT - red MUST be 128 along the mirror line. Neutralising red there therefore RESTORES the physically correct value rather than deleting sculpted detail, which is why it is safe, and why green needs no treatment at all (vertical slope does not flip across the fold; measured green change 0.0 bytes). This is the cheap fix for rule 87: texture-only, no FBX churn, no new material, zero draw-call cost.

92. BOUND A MIRROR-SEAM FEATHER BY THE NEAREST REAL ANATOMICAL FEATURE, not by whatever looks smooth. The philtrum ridges sit ~5 mm off the midline, so any feather wider than that flattens the philtrum - a worse artefact than the seam it fixes. Used: fully neutral within 1 mm (2 px), smoothstep to zero by 3 mm (7 px), at a measured 2.15 texels/mm. A pixel radius is meaningless until texel density is measured (rule 30/86).

93. REFINEMENT OF RULE 89. bpy.data.images.load() returns a datablock with has_data = False, and pixels.foreach_set then raises 'does not have any image data'. img.copy() fails the same way and cannot be revived by touching pixels. WORKING SEQUENCE: load(check_existing=False) -> read pixels[0] to force the buffer to materialise -> foreach_set -> update() -> file_format -> filepath_raw -> save(). Setting filepath_raw before the buffer exists is what breaks it. Cost two failed attempts on 2026-08-14.

94. VERIFY A MASKED TEXTURE EDIT WITH A MASK-INDEPENDENT INVARIANT, RE-READ FROM DISK. Re-applying your own mask only proves the code ran. For a neutralisation pass the invariants are: no texel moved AWAY from the target value (measured 0 of 4,194,304), the untouched channel changed by 0.0 bytes, and max change outside the mask = 0.0. Same discipline as the lip pass's zero-change check across 4,191,271 texels.

95. DEGENERATE UV TRIANGLES DO NOT BREAK TANGENTS - MEASURE BEFORE YOU CLAIM THEY DO. Measured on Yemoja_Body 2026-08-14: with 107 zero-area UV triangles present, mikktspace still returned 0 zero-length tangents, 0 NaNs, min length exactly 1.0. Blender and Unity both use mikktspace, so expect the same in engine. The real cost of a degenerate UV face is TEXTURE STRETCHING, not shading corruption. A 'divide-by-zero tangent' argument was asserted here and the control disproved it.

96. COUNT DEGENERATE UV TRIANGLES AFTER TRIANGULATION, NOT DEGENERATE FACES. 41 zero-UV-area faces produced 107 degenerate triangles, because 43 FURTHER quads carried a DUPLICATED UV CORNER - real UV area (median 1181 texels^2) but one of their two triangles empty. Faces and triangles are different populations and the exporter ships triangles. A face-level count understates the real number by 2.6x here.

97. calc_tangents() ABORTS ON N-GONS - 'Tangent space can only be computed for tris/quads, aborting' - and it aborts for the WHOLE MESH, so one n-gon blocks every tangent diagnostic. Yemoja_Body carries 70 n-gons (42 pentagons, 28 hexagons). To test tangents: copy the mesh, bmesh.ops.triangulate the COPY, calc_tangents on that, then remove it. Never triangulate the live mesh for a diagnostic. NOTE the 42 pentagons - that number probably explains the long-standing '42 degenerate-UV faces' entry, which never matched any UV measurement.

98. USE THE PRE-CHANGE SNAPSHOT AS A CONTROL, NOT JUST AS AN UNDO. bpy.data.libraries.load(snapshot) pulls the old datablock into the live session so before/after run through identical code. That is what disproved the tangent theory in rule 95 - a claim that had already been written into two handoff documents. Remove the appended object and purge orphans afterwards.

99. NEVER 'FIX' A SELF-INTERSECTING N-GON BY TRIANGULATING IT. BEAUTY triangulation draws diagonals between EXISTING boundary vertices, and on a hole cap those diagonals can coincide exactly with edges already present in the surrounding mesh - giving those edges 4 linked faces. Tried on Yemoja Hair 2026-08-14: self-intersection went 3 -> 0 but NON-MANIFOLD EDGES WENT 1 -> 5. Reverted from snapshot. If a cap ever genuinely must be fixed, POKE it instead (fan from a NEW centre vertex): every new edge then touches a vertex no other geometry shares, so it cannot go non-manifold.

100. UNITY DISCARDING A POLYGON IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A BUG TO FIX. The 3 self-intersecting hair caps (868-2241 mm2, top and back of the head) have been discarded on every Unity import since v2 and no hole has ever been seen. Four imports is real empirical evidence that they are interior geometry. Leaving them discarded is also a MOBILE WIN - keeping them would cost triangles and overdraw for something nobody can see. Fix what is visible, not what is merely untidy.

101. bpy.data.is_dirty IS NOT A SAVE SIGNAL. Script-driven edits do not push an undo step, and the dirty flag rides on that - it stayed False across a material reassignment, a texture repoint and a full node-rig build, and survived a connection restart still reading False while the changes were real and unsaved. It DOES fire correctly for hand edits in the UI. Blender will not prompt you on quit either. The reliable signal is the .blend file's mtime before and after bpy.ops.wm.save_mainfile(). Measured 2026-08-15.

102. REFINES 93. ASSIGNING image.colorspace_settings.name RELOADS THE BUFFER FROM THE SOURCE FILE AND SILENTLY UNDOES A PRIOR scale(). Cost two failed writes: img.scale(256,512) reported the new size correctly, then setting colorspace reverted it to 1024x1024, and foreach_set raised 'expected sequence size 4194304, got 524288' - an error that points at the write call three lines AFTER the actual cause. Correct order: load -> colorspace (and alpha_mode) -> read pixels[0] -> scale() -> foreach_set -> update() -> file_format -> filepath_raw -> save().

103. BEFORE AUTHORING ANY ROOT-TO-TIP GRADIENT, CORRELATE THE UV AXIS AGAINST 3D POSITION PER ISLAND, NOT GLOBALLY. On Yemoja Hair, V ran root-to-tip on 20 of 21 islands with correlations at or near -1.0, and the global correlation was a convincing -0.905. The exception - the hairline card - occupied V 0.553-0.732, where a V-driven gradient had already reached 1.005, so it was painted the BRIGHTEST value in the map while every other card darkened. A global correlation hides exactly the island that will fail.

104. A HEIGHT THRESHOLD IS A PLANE CUT; A SCALP IS A DOME. Driving root darkening from world Z over-covers and under-covers SIMULTANEOUSLY: the crown sits at z 7.3 so hair that had already swept far from its root went dark, while the temple scalp curves down to z 6.9, below the fade-out, so hair sitting AT its root got nothing. Use arc length travelled from the root along each card. Stored on Yemoja Hair as the POINT float attribute 'root_arclen' (0.0-3.7619 BU; median vertex 243.5 mm from its root, median card 784 mm). Computed per island by binning V, taking bin centroids and cumulating 3D distances between them. RECOMPUTE IT IF THE HAIR MESH EVER CHANGES.

105. OVERLAPPING UV ISLANDS MAKE POSITION-DEPENDENT BAKING AMBIGUOUS, AND IT FAILS SILENTLY. One texel serving two cards at different heights cannot hold two values; the last rasterised write wins with no warning. On Yemoja Hair, ALL 1,549 of the hairline card's texels lie inside island 1's footprint (a full-length loc), so every colour written for the hairline was overwritten by a loc and vice versa. Atlas-wide only 4.4% of used texels are shared and 13.4% is free, so relocation is cheap. MEASURE PER-TEXEL ISLAND SHARING BEFORE BAKING ANYTHING POSITION-DEPENDENT, and where overlap is unavoidable make NEAREST-TO-ROOT win rather than last-write.

106. EXTENDS 86. TEXEL DENSITY FOR ALPHA CARDS - COMPUTE THE CARD'S ON-SCREEN SIZE AGAINST THE TEXTURE STRIP IT SAMPLES BEFORE AUTHORING THE ALPHA. A hairline card ~22 px wide on screen sampling a 128 px strip is a 6x downsample. 641 strands at 1.6 px spacing and 0.7-1.5 px width averaged into SOLID GREY, so the visible silhouette became the QUAD EDGE and the cards read as cut-up strips of lash texture. Three iterations were spent tuning curl and density on detail that could never survive to the screen. Fewer, thicker strands win: 66 strands at 2.5-5.0 px dropped coverage 54.5% -> 29.5% and restored real gaps. Measured 2026-08-15.

107. AN ALPHA CARD'S TEXTURE MUST FADE TO ZERO AT ITS STRIP'S SIDE MARGINS, OR THE CARD'S OWN RECTANGLE BECOMES THE SILHOUETTE. If strands run to the edge of the UV strip, the quad's straight vertical borders are opaque and read as a cut edge no matter how good the strands are. A smoothstep window ~12-14 px wide at each strip margin fixes it, and costs nothing.

108. ANY CHAIN OR STOP CONDITION MUST TEST WHERE THE PLACED ELEMENT ENDS, NOT WHERE IT STARTS. Placing hairline cards while 'the current position is above the target line' let every chain run up to one full card length (25 mm) past the line. Clamp the element's length to the remaining distance instead: length = min(nominal, remaining / component_of_direction_along_the_limit).

109. RESTORING A DELETED ISLAND VIA bpy.data.libraries.load DUPLICATES BOUNDARY VERTS SHARED WITH SURVIVING GEOMETRY. Deleting the hairline card removed 386 of its 387 verts because one was also used by a neighbouring island; re-adding all 387 gave 4623 verts against an expected 4622, with faces and edges already correct. Weld ONLY cross-set coincident pairs (verts from the restored set within 1e-6 of a pre-existing vert). NEVER global merge-by-distance on this hair - it would undo the deliberate vertex split from the 2026-08-14d non-manifold fix (4620 -> 4622). Also note libraries.load selects by DATABLOCK name: the mesh is 'Yemoja_Hair_mesh', not 'Hair'; a name-guess falls through to df.meshes[0] and silently imports the wrong object.

110. A MESH SEPARATED OR DUPLICATED FROM A MIRRORED-UV BODY INHERITS THE OVERLAP AND CANNOT BE USED AS A HAIR OR SCATTER ATTACHMENT SURFACE UNTIL IT IS GIVEN A DEDICATED SECOND UV MAP. Yemoja_Scalp was duplicated out of Yemoja_Body and carried the skin atlas, which is 100% mirrored (see CRITICAL_mirrored_uv_atlas): measured 2026-08-15, all 67 mirror-paired verts shared BYTE-IDENTICAL UVs, delta exactly 0.0. Blender binds hair curves to a surface THROUGH the UV map, so a loc on her left can bind to the mirrored point on her right; nothing looks wrong until the head deforms and half the hair slides. This is rule 105 arriving through a different door - 105 is about BAKING being ambiguous, 110 is about ATTACHMENT being ambiguous. Fix: add a second UV layer used only for attachment, leave the skin atlas as active_render. For a scalp cap use a POLAR PROJECTION onto a UV disc (r = polar angle from the head-centre axis / max, theta = azimuth) - it has NO U-wrap seam, so no face carries wrapped coordinates. Verify with three numbers: zero negative-area UV faces (no folds), zero zero-area faces, and a non-zero minimum vertex UV separation. COROLLARY: that separation test also detects DOUBLED VERTS in the source mesh - it found 4 coincident pairs at 0.00mm on Yemoja_Scalp that had produced 2 degenerate quads. Yemoja_Body itself was clean (0 coincident, 0 zero-area), so the doubles came from the duplicate/separate operation, not from the body.

111. YEMOJA HAIR STYLE SPEC - MEASURED FROM THE ORIGINAL 'Hair' MESH, DO NOT RE-DERIVE BY EYE. Stephanie's approved flow, measured 2026-08-16 over the old mesh's 17 loc islands: locs sweep DOWN and BACK at a ratio of backward/down = 0.243 (median +Y 0.475 BU against -Z 1.951 BU), with radial fan-out of essentially ZERO (median -0.038). She elected to KEEP radial spread at 0.22 in the new generator anyway, for silhouette width, so the generator's SWEEP coefficient is 0.13 not 0.243 - spread already contributes backward motion on the rear locs and the measured value double-counts. Target: tip-minus-root Y median ~0.50. Locs must NOT fall over her face. Roots sink 10mm INSIDE the scalp so the tube end-caps hide under the fuzz shell. Long locs are deliberate (water-goddess persona) - do not shorten to solve body clipping.

112. BLENDER 5.2 GEOMETRY NODES API TRAPS - ALL FOUND THE HARD WAY 2026-08-16. (a) The Nodes modifier NO LONGER stores input values as IDProperties: md['Socket_N'] raises TypeError and md.keys() raises outright. (b) Consequently, clearing and rebuilding ng.interface ORPHANS every stored modifier value and the tree silently runs at socket MINIMUMS - spacing 0, 1 segment, 3-sided profile - with NO node warning emitted. Symptom is thousands of degenerate 3-vert/2-face slivers. Fix is to remove and re-add the modifier. (c) THEREFORE: expose controls as labelled RIG_ Value nodes INSIDE the group, not as group inputs - settable from Python, draggable by Stephanie, immune to the orphaning bug. (d) GeometryNodeInputSplineParameter is renamed GeometryNodeSplineParameter. (e) Curve to Mesh has an explicit Scale input that SUPERSEDES the curve radius attribute - Set Curve Radius is ignored; a 1.0 profile circle renders 240mm-wide tubes. (f) FLOAT2 attribute elements use foreach_set('vector'), not 'value'. (g) Store Named Attribute carries a hidden Value socket per data type, all named 'Value' - select by socket .type, never by name. (h) RNA structs return a NEW Python wrapper on every access, so 'link.from_node is my_node' is ALWAYS False - compare by .name.

113. GEOMETRY CANNOT CARRY COIL AT GAME SEGMENT COUNTS - STOP CHASING IT. The original hair mesh has an arc/chord ratio of 1.71 (arc 810mm over a 475mm chord) because its cards zigzag finely. At 12-16 points per loc the achievable ratio is ~1.02; raising the wave amplitude from 0.15 to 0.25 moved it from 1.018 to 1.021, i.e. nothing. Reaching 1.71 would need ~40mm amplitude over a 158mm wavelength, which reads as a flapping ribbon, not coil. DIVISION OF LABOUR: geometry carries the SWEEP and the HANG; the NORMAL MAP carries the coil. Same conclusion the fuzz-shell analysis reached from the opposite direction.

114. RULE 106 CUTS BOTH WAYS - DO NOT AUTHOR DETAIL COARSER THAN REALITY EITHER. First coil sheet was built at 5.0mm so individual coils would clear the 2px floor at fight camera; real 4C coil pitch is 2-3mm. Result read as flat concentric fossils at BOTH distances. 106 forbids detail FINER than the downsample can carry; it never licensed inflating detail past its true physical scale. Detail that blurs to TONE at distance and resolves up close is the correct outcome. v2 sheet: 2.5mm pitch, 420 kinked overlapping strands (NOT Archimedean spirals - those read as ammonites), max slope 61 deg against v1's 31. Measured reference: scalp is 130.1mm wide, 492 cm2; at 400px character height that is 29.3 screen px and 4.44 mm/px.

makeup_layer.architecture: Makeup is a TEXTURE VARIANT, not a runtime layer. Keep Yemoja_Color_SkinGrade_v1.png pristine and never paint into it; author an RGBA overlay; composite the two into a variant base-colour PNG that Unity swaps per skin. Zero runtime cost - no extra texture sample, shader branch, draw call or geometry.
makeup_layer.status: SUPERSEDED by the eyeliner decal mesh (2026-08-08) - see eyeliner_decal. The texture-variant approach remains valid for makeup that is NOT a crisp line (blush, shadow washes), which the atlas density can carry.
makeup_layer.BLOCKER_uv_resolution: The upper lid margin occupies only ~16 x 50 TEXELS in the skin atlas. The lash line is ~50 texels long. No eyeliner painted into the skin atlas can be crisp at that density - procedurally OR by hand. Measure the available UV space BEFORE designing any detail for a region.
makeup_layer.recommended_solution: A separate makeup DECAL MESH: a thin strip over the lid with its own material and its own UV space, so the liner gets a full texture region. Also not mirrored, so asymmetric designs become possible. Cost ~40-80 verts plus one draw call. Hide the object for the natural face; swap its texture per skin.

eyeliner_decal.why_a_decal: The upper lid margin occupies only ~16x50 texels in the skin atlas and the body atlas is 100% mirrored, so no painted eyeliner can be crisp or asymmetric. A decal mesh gets its own UV space and is not mirrored. Four texture passes were wasted proving this first - see rule 30.
eyeliner_decal.construction: Path derived from lash root points, fitted with a robust degree-4 polynomial in t (outliers beyond 2.5x median residual dropped - they are the pre-existing flat shards at the inner corner), resampled evenly by arc length, then swept as a 2-vertex-wide strip. Upper path 25.9mm over 25 rings plus a 6-ring wing; lower path 19.0mm over 22 rings.
eyeliner_decal.seating: Radially outward from the eye centre via ray casts, then HAND-FITTED by Stephanie (see rule 31). She settled on ~0.9mm clearance, deeper than the 0.36mm first tried.
eyeliner_decal.material: Yemoja_Eyeliner_mat, SHARED by both objects - one draw call for all four lines. FINAL: base colour #8FC4DA pale ice-blue (linear 0.2747, 0.5520, 0.7011), roughness 0.15, metallic 0. URP equivalent: _Smoothness 0.85. Needs NO alpha texture - the mesh silhouette is the shape, unlike the lash cards whose shape is painted into their texture. Material kept to Base Color + Metallic + Roughness ONLY so the Blender preview matches what URP Lit can actually reproduce - a Coat layer looks better in Blender and cannot ship.
eyeliner_decal.skinning: single vertex group mixamorig:Head at weight 1.0, Mirror BEFORE Armature - same setup as the lash cards.
eyeliner_decal.mirror: Mirror modifier referencing Yemoja_Body, use_mirror_merge False. Upper base half is -x, lower base half is +x (see rule 34).
eyeliner_decal.colour_rationale: Black gave the crispest cat-eye but framed a teal iris with a hard graphic. Pure white FAILED - it merges with the white lashes and the wing shape disappears. Pale ice-blue separates from both the warm skin and the warm-white lashes, and sits next to the iris hue so the eye reads as one cool zone. Trade-off accepted: the upper and lower lines now carry similar visual weight rather than the upper wing dominating.
eyeliner_decal.sheen_note: Roughness 0.15 barely reads in a static frame: the strip is near-flat so its normal hardly varies across 1-2mm and there is no angle range for a highlight to land in. It pays off in MOTION (head turns on select screen / victory poses). To make it read statically, roll the strip's outer edge a few degrees off the lid - geometry change, hand-fit per rule 31. On mobile with no reflection probe the sheen comes almost entirely off the main directional light, so the select-screen lighting rig decides whether it shows.

CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.what: Yemoja_Body is skinned almost entirely to the .R bone set on BOTH halves of the body.
CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.evidence: Total vertex weight .L = 13.25 vs .R = 4098.14. Only 2 of 23 .L groups carry any weight (Shoulder.L 0.44, UpLeg.L 12.81). Probed mirrored vertex pairs: world x +1.812 and -1.821 both report mixamorig:Hand.R at weight 0.939. Both thighs report UpLeg.R at 1.0.
CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.scope: Yemoja_Body ONLY. Yemoja_Clothes is correctly sided (L 2159.05 / R 2082.04, 8 groups each side). Hair uses hair_loc bones and is unaffected.
CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.already_in_unity: YES. The exported Yemoja_v2.fbx carries the identical fault (L 13.25 / R 4098.17). Not introduced by the 2026-08-12 sculpt.
CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.why_nobody_noticed: Bind pose is correct and the idle is near-symmetric. Unity-side checks were avatar-level (isHuman, bone rotation, retarget) and do not test skin weights.
CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.expected_symptom: On any non-symmetric animation the body's left arm and left leg follow the RIGHT bones, while the clothes on those limbs follow correctly - so the body and its garments visibly separate.
CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.likely_cause: A mirror/symmetrize of weights that copied without flipping the .L/.R suffix. This naming-sensitive failure is exactly what the project-wide rename to Blender convention was meant to prevent.
CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.fix: Re-mirror vertex groups on Yemoja_Body only, with proper L/R suffix flipping. Verify by re-summing total weight per side (should come out roughly balanced, as the clothes do) and by re-probing mirrored vertex pairs.
CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.resolved_how: Rebuilt every +x (her left) vertex's weights from its local-space mirror partner on -x, flipping .L/.R on the way across. Chosen over a plain suffix rename because near-centreline verts legitimately blend both sides and a rename would collide on them; mirroring maps a partner's 0.5/0.2 to 0.2/0.5 correctly. 3264 verts rebuilt. The 133 centreline verts were left untouched - 18 of them already carried correct dual L/R weighting and were the only surviving legitimate .L weight.
CRITICAL_skin_weight_fault.resolved_verification: Totals now L 2056.68 / R 2054.74 (imbalance 1.94, better than the clothes' 77); 23 of 23 .L groups carry weight. Mirrored pair now reports DIFFERENT dominant bones - HandMiddle2.R at -x, HandMiddle2.L at +x, both 0.82. Per-vertex weight sums unchanged (min 1.0 / median 1.0 / max 3.0, same 226 non-normalised verts), proving weight was moved between groups and not recomputed, so deformation shape is untouched. hair_realism_investigation_2026_08_14.current_setup: Yemoja_Hair_mat = flat Base Color (0.7137, 0.7325, 0.7476), CONSTANT Roughness 0.7012, Metallic 0, Alpha 1.0 (fully OPAQUE, no transparency), and ONE 1024 normal map (Yemoja_Hair_Normal.png, Non-Color). That is the whole material. Mesh: 4,622 verts / 4,391 faces / 9,029 tris, one UV layer, 45 hair bones, one material.
hair_realism_investigation_2026_08_14.FINDING_1_the_normal_map_is_good_but_ROT: This is the prime suspect and it is measured, not guessed. TWO independent tests agree the map has ONE dominant direction at about 45-60 deg in texture space: (a) slope-vector orientation histogram - 194,777 of ~262,000 strong pixels in the single 45-60 deg bin, peak ratio 8.9; (b) autocorrelation - correlation length 31 px along ~50 deg vs 5 px across, i.e. features are 6:1 ELONGATED, so these are genuine strands, not grain. MEANWHILE THE CARDS RUN AT 90 deg: median UV long-axis 90.1 deg, 3,136 of 4,314 quads inside 75-105 deg. So the strands in the texture cross the strands in the geometry at roughly 40 deg. That is what diagonal-scratch hair looks like.
hair_realism_investigation_2026_08_14.FINDING_2_it_is_NOT_a_blotch_map: Unlike the base colour and roughness maps that rules 67-69 correctly rejected, this normal map is genuinely high frequency: at a 128 px block split, 0.0% of variance is low frequency (R and G). Do NOT throw it away - it is good data pointed the wrong way.
hair_realism_investigation_2026_08_14.FINDING_3_roughness_is_uniform_RULE_88: Hair roughness is a CONSTANT 0.7012. Rule 88 was learned on the lips: uniform roughness reads as plastic. The identical fault is present on the hair and nobody has looked at it. Low-frequency breakup is the cheapest possible fix and, being scalar, is immune to rule 87 mirroring problems.
hair_realism_investigation_2026_08_14.FINDING_4_atlas_is_94_pct_empty: Hair occupies only 5.6% of its 1024 UV atlas (cards stacked, max 86 loops in one cell - normal for hair cards). Texel density along a card is 1.74 texels/mm median. If the map is ever regenerated, a small TILING strip would do the same job for a fraction of the texture memory - a mobile win in the spirit of rule 69.
RECOMMENDED_ORDER: 1. CHEAPEST, HIGHEST VALUE, TEXTURE-ONLY, NO RE-EXPORT: realign the normal map's strand direction to the card direction (~40 deg). CRITICAL: rotating a normal map is NOT just rotating pixels - the RG vector components must be rotated by the same angle or every slope points the wrong way. Alternatively regenerate the streaks procedurally aligned to +V, using the same technique as the leather-grain and skin-pore detail maps. Either way this needs Stephanie's eye, not a measurement, to confirm.

2. CHEAP, TEXTURE-ONLY: add low-frequency roughness breakup (rule 88). Costs one small greyscale map, or pack it alongside something existing. Uniform roughness is why it reads as plastic rather than hair.

3. MEDIUM: root-to-tip value gradient. Real hair is darker at the roots and the base colour is currently a flat constant. Cheapest route is a generated gradient map - note this does NOT violate rules 67-69, which are about not rescuing the MODELLER's flat-fill atlas, not about refusing to generate a good one.

4. PROBABLY OUT OF SCOPE FOR MOBILE: anisotropic specular. Real hair's highlight stretches along the strand; URP Lit has no anisotropy, so it needs a custom Shader Graph. Flag for the AAA copy, not this deliverable.
hair_realism_investigation_2026_08_14.DO_NOT_DO_alpha_cards: Do NOT add alpha-tested wispy tips to make the silhouette softer. The hair is currently fully OPAQUE and its silhouette comes from geometry. Alpha means overdraw, and per this project's own note overdraw - not vertex count - is a binding mobile constraint. Keep this for the AAA copy.

new_mesh_attribute.name: root_arclen
new_mesh_attribute.meaning: 3D arc length travelled from each card's own root.
new_mesh_attribute.method: Per UV island: bin loops by V, take the 3D centroid of each bin, cumulate distances between consecutive centroids, interpolate per loop. Nearest-to-root wins where a vert has several loops.
new_mesh_attribute.stats: median vertex 243.5 mm from its root, furthest 902.3 mm, median card length 784 mm.
new_mesh_attribute.WARNING: Recompute from scratch if the hair mesh changes. It is also a custom attribute - decide whether it should ship in the FBX.

geometry_nodes_plan.trap_1_uv_overlap: Its UVs lie ENTIRELY inside island 1's footprint - see rule 105. Any position-dependent texture work on it is ambiguous until it gets its own UV space. 13.4% of the atlas is free.
geometry_nodes_plan.trap_2_material: It is on Yemoja_Hair_mat, which is OPAQUE. Fuzz needs alpha. Do NOT add alpha to Yemoja_Hair_mat - that makes all 4,053 loc faces transparent, a serious overdraw hit. Cheapest route is the existing Yemoja_Lashes_mat (DITHERED, threshold 0.4), which the brow rebuild proved costs zero new materials and zero new draw calls. But that sheet is near-white and Stephanie wants the edges DARKER than the locs, which means its own atlas region - budget for growing the sheet again.
geometry_nodes_plan.trap_3_direction: Do NOT project world -Z onto the surface for a 'down the forehead' direction - on the crown the normal points nearly straight up, the projection collapses and the direction becomes unstable. That is why one build's fuzz flowed backward into the locs. Aim at a point on the face, or use GN's own surface-tangent handling.
geometry_nodes_plan.target_shape: Hairline at world z ~7.07 at centre, descending toward the temples, approx z = 7.07 - 0.55 * max(0, |x| - 0.10). The fuzz must COVER the band from the loc roots down to that line - a filled band, not a fringe of separate tufts. Forehead PLUS temples/sideburns. Reference: a dense band of very short tightly-coiled fuzz close to the scalp with a soft diffuse edge - NOT wispy, NOT lash-like. Direction mixed/halo, radiating rather than combed.
